title: A king once stood before God and was offered anything.
paragraphs: A king once stood before God and was offered anything.

Power.
Revenge.
Riches beyond imagination.
But what he asked for shocked heaven.

Not gold.
Not victory.
Not fame.
Wisdom.
And that moment changed history.
Picture the scene.
Night. Silence. The sacred stillness of Gibeon. The smoke of sacrifices still rising. A young king kneels beneath the stars, the weight of an entire nation pressing on his shoulders.
This is Solomon.

He is not old.
He is not seasoned.
He has just inherited the throne of his father David.

A kingdom is watching him.
Enemies are watching him.
History is waiting.
Then God speaks.
“Ask what I shall give you.” (1 Kings 3:5)
Think about that.
The Creator of the universe looks at a human being and says:
“What do you want?”
That question exposes the heart.
Because what we ask for reveals what we worship.

Most people would ask for power.
Some would ask for wealth.
Others would ask for their enemies to fall.
But Solomon answered with a confession that shook heaven.

“I am only a little child and do not know how to carry out my duties…
Give your servant a discerning heart.”
— 1 Kings 3:7–9
In other words:
“God… I’m not enough for this.”
That is the birthplace of wisdom.

Not brilliance.
Not intellect.
Not education.
Humility.

Wisdom begins when a person finally admits:
“I cannot lead this life without God.”
And the Bible says something astonishing.

“The Lord was pleased that Solomon had asked for this.”
— 1 Kings 3:10
God delights when a heart chooses wisdom over power.
So God answered.
Not just wisdom.
Overflow.

“I will give you a wise and discerning heart…
I will also give you what you did not ask for—both wealth and honor.”
— 1 Kings 3:12–13
Did you catch that?
When Solomon asked for what honored God, God took care of the rest.
This is a pattern across Scripture.

Seek first the kingdom…
and everything else finds its proper place.
But here is the deeper truth most people miss.
Even Solomon—the wisest king who ever lived—eventually drifted.
His wisdom was real.
But wisdom alone could not save him from sin.

His heart slowly divided.
Foreign loves crept in.
Idols appeared.
The wisest man on earth still needed a Savior.
And that is where the story points beyond Solomon.
Because centuries later, another King would come.
Not merely wise.
Wisdom itself in flesh.
That King is Jesus Christ.
Jesus said something remarkable:

“Something greater than Solomon is here.”
— Matthew 12:42
Solomon asked for wisdom.
Jesus is wisdom.
Solomon needed guidance.
Jesus guides the lost.
Solomon ruled a kingdom.
Jesus rules eternity.

And unlike Solomon, Jesus never drifted.
Never sinned.
Never compromised.
He carried the weight of humanity's failure… all the way to the cross.
There, the greater King did something Solomon never could.
He paid for sin.
He defeated death.
He opened the door for every broken heart to be made new.
So the lesson of 1 Kings 3 is not simply:
“Try to be wise.”
The deeper invitation is this:
Come to the One who is wisdom.
Because life will place crowns on your head that you cannot carry alone.

Leadership.
Marriage.
Parenthood.
Ministry.
Business.
Influence.
Every blessing becomes dangerous without God.
Position without wisdom becomes destruction.
But there is hope.
James writes:
— James 1:5
God is not stingy with wisdom.
He gives it generously.

To the humble.
To the seeking.
To those who admit their need.
So today ask yourself an honest question:

If God appeared tonight and asked,
“What do you want me to give you?”
What would your heart say?
Money?
Success?
Control?
Or wisdom?
Because the answer to that question may reveal the direction of your soul.

And if your heart whispers,
“Lord… I don’t know how to live this life well.”
That is not weakness.
That is the beginning of wisdom.
And the good news is this:
Through Jesus, you can approach God boldly.
Not as someone who has everything figured out…
But as someone who knows exactly where wisdom comes from.
So pray this simple prayer today:

“Lord, give me a listening heart.
Not just knowledge… but wisdom.
Not just success… but surrender.
Lead me in the way of Christ.”
Because the greatest kings are not the ones who know everything.
They are the ones who know who to ask.
And when you ask God for wisdom…
He just might change the entire story of your life.
Someone you know may need this reminder today.
And remember:
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
